messages:
Rosa L.: Quick alert — p99 in eu-west jumped at ~02:12 UTC, correlating with a flurry of dedicated pool advertisements. Looks like warm-pool announce -> immediate traffic shift -> fallback to smaller models. Anyone on-call?
Ken H.: Saw it. dashboard shows advertise_count spiking then fallback_count rising ~30s later. Network looks fine but proxy metrics show a handful of `accept_tx_errors`.
infra-bot: ALERT: dedicated-advertise-spike (eu-west). advertise_count=112 window=5m, fallback_count=58, severity=warning
Nima P.: We recently enabled aggressive warmup in rollout-9 to cut cold starts. Possible the advertise happens before slot completes state sync (kv cache). Proxy treats the slot as available and routing flips.
SRE Oncall: Do we have tenant-level winners here? Which tenants caused fallbacks?
Ken H.: Tenant breakdown: search-service 42% of fallback traffic, embed-ops 22%, misc 36%. search had a hot batch of small requests.
Rosa L.: Proposed quick change: add an `advertise_grace_ms` and pilot 10s delay for eu-west canary, plus track `route.accept_ack` metric. Short config patch below: 
```
service.route.advertise_grace_ms = 10000
service.route.require_accept_ack = true
```
That `require_accept_ack` flips routing only after proxy ack.
Nima P.: require_accept_ack sounds safer but could reintroduce cold penalties if accept ack is slow. We should also instrument how long accept ack takes under load.
Ken H.: Test plan: 1) flip advertise_grace_ms=10s in single rack canary; 2) enable accept_ack for canary; 3) run synthetic p99 soak for 20m; 4) monitor egress bytes and cost delta.
SRE Oncall: Also add alert: if fallback_count rises >50% baseline in 5m, auto-disable prefer-warm flag for that rack. We should auto-protect tenants rather than manual rollbacks.
Rosa L.: Agreed. I'll open INFRA ticket and add an auto-toggle in the playbook.
infra-bot: DEPLOYMENT: config/warmup v3.7 -> canary-rack-7 started by Rosa L. at 02:35 UTC
Ken H.: Canary after 8m: fallback_count down 68%, p99 returned to baseline, advertise_grace_ms trimmed surges. Small cost bump (~0.4%) during sync but projected savings after reduced fallbacks.
Nima P.: Good. Follow-ups: instrument `accept_ack_latency_ms` histogram and add unit tests for advertise/accept race. Also add per-tenant fallback alert and a quick kill-switch.
SRE Oncall: I'll encode the alert as: `rate(fallback_count{rack=\"eu-west\"}[5m]) > 1.5 * baseline` -> runbook jump to auto-disable prefer-warm.
Rosa L.: Ticket INFRA-2410 created and linked: https://redwood.internal/infra/INFRA-2410. Drafting short note to product about the temporary latency/cost tradeoff.
Ken H.: Thanks. Rolling to eu-west with staged batches if no regressions in 40m.
Nima P.: Also flag for future: consider a soft-quarantine approach where newly-advertised slots get a low-weight routing share for a brief window instead of full promotion. That might smooth tail without full disable.
Rosa L.: Noted. Will add to infra backlog. Closing canary watch — will report in 40m.
SRE Oncall: :thumbsup: keeping watch on alerts.
infra-bot: NOTE: canary stable at 40m. rolling to remaining eu-west racks."
